priorStories.headline: U.S. adds AI-chip export and remote-access controls
priorStories.body:
The Commerce Department issued rules Monday requiring export licenses for covered advanced-AI-chip shipments to Singapore, Thailand, Malaysia, Indonesia and Brazil, Reuters reported. U.S. companies operating data centers in those countries are exempt from that shipment requirement.

Separately, overseas data centers providing significant computing power to companies headquartered in China must obtain licenses within 90 days to continue those services or face future export restrictions. That provision is not an immediate prohibition on all remote computing services.

The regulation also formally rescinds the Biden-era global AI-chip licensing rule.

priorStories.headline: EU sanctions nearly 50 Russian financial institutions
priorStories.body:
The European Union imposed Russia-related sanctions on 145 people and entities Monday, including nearly 50 Russian banks and financial institutions.

One set of measures targeted 12 people and 101 entities linked to financing Russia's war in Ukraine and the shadow fleet. Another covered 30 people and two entities linked to information manipulation and cyberattacks, including the Social Design Agency and hacker group NoName057(16).

These sanctions were adopted by the Council; a further sanctions package remained under preparation.

sources.name: Council of the European Union — war-financing sanctions
Council of the European Union — information manipulation and cyber sanctions

candidates.summary: President Donald Trump arrived at Manila's Ninoy Aquino International Airport at 5:33 p.m. Philippine time (09:33 UTC) on November 17. Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent accompanied him. The arrival began the Philippine stop of his Asia trip; subsequent meetings and agreements were not yet established as completed by the reporting reviewed.
candidates.title: Trump arrives in Manila for Philippine stop of Asia trip

candidates.summary: Bahrain's Defence Force announced November 17 that it had intercepted and destroyed Iranian aerial attacks. Iran's Revolutionary Guard said it launched drones targeting a U.S.-operated radar system at Sheikh Isa Air Base. Bahrain's Interior Ministry subsequently announced an all-clear following a threat alert. The reviewed reporting did not independently establish Iran's claim of a successful strike on the radar facility.
candidates.title: Bahrain reports intercepting Iranian aerial attacks; Iran claims U.S. radar target

candidates.summary: The Office for National Statistics released November labour-market figures showing provisional UK payroll employment fell by 34,000 between September and October, to 30.2 million. Vacancies fell by 22,000 over the quarter to August–October, to 690,000. Survey-based unemployment was estimated at 4.6% in July–September, down 0.3 percentage points on the quarter, but ONS cautioned that survey-sample rotation partly explained that decline. Annual regular earnings growth slowed to 3.5%, from 3.7% in the preceding three-month period.
candidates.title: UK payroll employment and vacancies fall as wage growth slows

candidates.summary: The Census Bureau released October retail and food-services sales estimates at 8:30 a.m. EST on November 17. Seasonally adjusted sales were $748.2 billion, up an estimated 0.2% from September and 6.8% from October 2025. The monthly estimate's 90% confidence interval included zero, so the reported increase was not statistically distinguishable from no change. September's 0.8% monthly increase was unrevised. The figures are not adjusted for price changes.
candidates.title: U.S. October retail sales estimated up 0.2%, with monthly change statistically uncertain

candidates.summary: The Federal Reserve's November 17 release showed industrial production decreased 0.4% in October after increasing 0.7% in September. Manufacturing output rose 0.3%, while mining output fell 0.8% and utilities output fell 4.3%. Manufacturing excluding motor vehicles and parts edged down 0.1%. Overall capacity utilization declined to 76.4%, three percentage points below its 1972–2025 average. Total industrial production remained 2.1% above its year-earlier level.
candidates.title: U.S. industrial production falls 0.4% in October as utilities output declines

candidates.summary: The Bureau of Labor Statistics reported November 17 that U.S. import prices increased 1.1% in October, matching September's monthly increase, Reuters reported. These price indexes exclude tariffs. BLS did not publish an October year-over-year import-price comparison because the federal government shutdown had prevented collection of October 2025 data.
candidates.title: U.S. import prices rise 1.1% in October

candidates.summary: In a November 17 statement reported by Reuters at 6:25 a.m. EST, President Volodymyr Zelenskiy confirmed Ukraine had attacked the Crimea bridge with drones and missiles. He described the strike as the seventh stage of a weeks-long operation coordinated by the SBU security service and General Staff, following attacks on Russian defensive systems. He said the operation targeted both road and rail sections. Reuters' initial report could not independently verify imagery he published appearing to show the main road arch collapsed into the Kerch Strait.
candidates.title: Zelenskiy confirms Ukrainian Crimea bridge operation and describes its preparation

candidates.summary: President Donald Trump arrived in Manila at 5:33 p.m. Philippine time on November 17, accompanied by Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent. A joint statement confirms that Trump subsequently met Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese, Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Japanese Prime Minister Takaichi Sanae for a Quad summit. The leaders announced a maritime-surveillance collaboration and enhanced cybersecurity cooperation. Their statement described a Quad maritime aircraft exercise as scheduled for 2027, not already completed.
candidates.title: Trump arrives in Manila and meets Quad leaders
candidates.geography: Philippines; United States; Australia; India; Japan

sources.name: Japan Ministry of Foreign Affairs — Quad joint statement

candidates.summary: Nvidia announced November 17 that revenue for its fiscal third quarter ended October 25 reached $115.8 billion, up 20% from the preceding quarter and 103% from a year earlier. Data Center revenue was $107.6 billion, up 110% year over year. The company reported GAAP diluted earnings per share of $2.70 and a GAAP gross margin of 74.8%. Colette Kress issued the results as interim chief executive and chief financial officer.
candidates.title: Nvidia reports $115.8 billion in quarterly revenue

sources.name: U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission — Nvidia Form 8-K

candidates.summary: Nvidia announced November 17 that its board had established a standing National Security and Export Control Oversight Committee. The company said the committee would oversee national-security policies, export-control compliance and global trade risk management.
candidates.title: Nvidia establishes board committee for national security and export controls

candidates.summary: Reuters reported November 17 that the Wall Street Journal, citing people familiar with the matter, said the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission was probing Nvidia following Jensen Huang's resignation as chief executive. The reviewed Reuters account did not establish when the investigation began or report an enforcement finding.
candidates.title: Reuters relays report of SEC investigation into Nvidia

candidates.summary: Michigan Attorney General Dana Nessel announced November 17 that she intended to request another Energy Department rehearing over an order requiring the J.H. Campbell coal plant to operate until February 12, 2027. The department issued that seventh order on Friday, rather than November 17. Nessel cited a September 11 appellate ruling vacating the department's first Campbell order and disputed the asserted energy emergency. Her announcement described an intended challenge, not a newly completed filing or court ruling.
candidates.title: Michigan attorney general announces intended challenge to latest Campbell coal-plant order

candidates.summary: SELLAS Life Sciences announced November 17 that its randomized Phase 3 REGAL trial of galinpepimut-S met its overall-survival endpoint. The company reported median survival of 24.0 months versus 14.7 months with best available treatment, a hazard ratio of 0.59 and p=0.035. The trial studied maintenance treatment for acute myeloid leukemia patients in second or later remission who could not undergo an allogeneic stem-cell transplant. These were company-reported topline results; the announcement described preparations for a regulatory application, not FDA approval.
candidates.title: SELLAS reports positive topline survival results from Phase 3 leukemia trial

sources.name: SELLAS Life Sciences — company news release

GAAP diluted earnings per share were $2.70 and gross margin was 74.8%. Colette Kress issued the results as interim chief executive and chief financial officer. On the subsequent earnings call, board Chairman Harvey Jones said the board did not intend to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO, after Huang publicly expressed willingness to return earlier Tuesday.

sources.name: U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission — Nvidia Form 8-K

candidates.summary: Reuters reported November 17, citing three people familiar with the matter, that President Donald Trump had withdrawn Heidi Overton's nomination to lead the Food and Drug Administration because of insufficient congressional support. The withdrawal preceded a scheduled Senate committee vote. Two sources said the White House was considering Senator Roger Marshall as a replacement; the report did not establish that a replacement nomination had been made.
candidates.title: Reuters reports withdrawal of Heidi Overton's FDA nomination

candidates.summary: An internal classified communications network used by National Security Agency employees experienced disruption November 17. The NSA attributed the temporary degradation to scheduled routine maintenance and said mission-critical capabilities remained operational. Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton said officials saw no indication of a coordinated cyberattack or state-sponsored activity behind recent technology outages. Secretary of State Marco Rubio likewise described the incidents as unrelated technical failures. These were officials' assessments, not an independently established common explanation for every outage.
candidates.title: NSA reports maintenance-related network disruption; officials reject coordinated-attack explanation

candidates.summary: PAHO announced November 17 that Bolivia, Mexico and the United States had lost measles-elimination status following a regional commission review held November 10–13 and acceptance of its recommendations by PAHO's director. The organization said the same virus lineage had circulated uninterrupted for at least 12 months in each country, re-establishing endemic transmission. PAHO urged stronger vaccination, surveillance and outbreak response. The announcement did not mean that every country in the Americas had endemic transmission.
candidates.title: PAHO announces loss of measles-elimination status in Bolivia, Mexico and United States

candidates.summary: The House Foreign Affairs Committee announced November 17 that former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang had agreed to a December 1 transcribed interview before three House committees investigating national-security concerns involving Nvidia. Later Tuesday, a spokesperson for Senate Banking Committee Chairman Tim Scott confirmed Huang had also agreed to testify before that panel. Reporting did not establish a confirmed Senate hearing date; Scott's earlier request had proposed December 3. Neither congressional appearance had occurred by the end of November 17.
candidates.title: Huang agrees to House interview and Senate Banking Committee testimony
